thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — ILB control-plane / route propagation anomaly observed impacting Private VPC cross-region routing (us-east1 <-> eu-west1). Multiple private-vpc tenants reporting 502/connection failures and asymmetric routing. GCP incident suspected. https://status.cloud.google.com/ — filing case now.

sara: seeing huge spike in 502s from our ILB frontends to eu backends. latency up, a percent of requests failing. throwing 502s from envoy.

mike: running quick checks against ILB health checks and forwarding rules. one backend group in eu-west1 shows health failing for ~40% of backends.

mike: ```
$ gcloud compute forwarding-rules list --filter="region:(us-east1 eu-west1)" --format="table(name,region,IPAddress)"
NAME                REGION    IPADDRESS
redwood-ilb-us      us-east1  10.50.1.23
redwood-ilb-eu      eu-west1  10.51.4.56
```

raj: also seeing route propagation inconsistencies; some routes from control plane to ilb backends not propagating to the eu routers. BGP-like control plane delay.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: On-call sara (ack) — case created with GCP (case# 2026-3871). Severity P1. Conference bridge spawned: https://meet.redwood/incident-1893456789

opsbot: :eyes: Posted initial customer-impact banner to status.redwood.com (Private VPC customers in eu-us cross-region).

liz: Hey @tanya — can you prep a short customer note? need to list impacted regions and suggested mitigations.

tanya: drafting — will include affected customers, temporary workarounds (add regional backends, avoid cross-region failover), and ETA for next update.

mike: quick mitigation attempt: cycling ILB backends in eu-west1 to force re-registration with control plane. patch command: ```bash
for i in $(gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels.ilb-backend=redwood" --regions=eu-west1 --format="value(name)"); do gcloud compute instances reset $i --zone europe-west1-b; done
```

sara: doing on-call handoff in 10m. @mike you take primary after that. set notification policy to page for increases >5% error rate.

raj: GCP support says this is a known internal control-plane routing regression affecting ILB route fanout across regions. they're rolling a targeted fix to control plane — ETA 25-40m.

cody: can we short-circuit by forcing traffic to stay regional? For private-vpc customers we could flip routing policy at the edge to prefer local backends until propagation stabilizes. That requires config push to 3 tenants to avoid broad churn.

mike: low-risk plan: 1) prefer regional backend for all traffic from entry region, 2) increase health-check retry window to avoid transient failures triggering removal, 3) monitor for 15m. I'm pushing config to canary tenants now.

liz: pushed canary change to 2 tenants -> no change in error rate yet for them, but they were at lower load.

tanya: customer comms update sent to impacted accounts, added link to status page and mitigation steps.

incident-bot: GCP updated case: rolling control-plane deploy started in eu-west1/us-east1. monitoring route propagation.

mike: health checks in eu-west1 beginning to recover, backend counts climbing back to expected.

sara: handing off to mike for overnight, I'm OOO after 03:00 UTC. mike you're primary.

mike: taking over — oncall takeover noted in PD. will stay till stabilization.

raj: route table dump after partial fix: ```
ROUTE: redwood-ilb-eu -> propagated: true -> next_hop: control-plane-eu -> status: ACTIVE
ROUTE: redwood-ilb-us -> propagated: true -> next_hop: control-plane-us -> status: ACTIVE
```

opsbot: :white_check_mark: Monitoring: error rate dropped from 8.2% -> 0.6% over last 12m. Latency trending down.

incident-bot: GCP confirms targeted rollback of the offending control-plane change completed, propagation returning to normal. Case updated.

tanya: preparing final customer update that notes: root cause suspected GCP control-plane route propagation regression, mitigation: GCP rollback + our regional preference toggles, next steps: follow up postmortem and recommendations for customers to configure regional failover limits.

mike: will keep monitoring for 60m. if metrics stable, escalate to incident review.

cody: filed internal blameless postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-1219 — will include timeline and suggested infra hardening (route propagation alerts, automated regional-preference fallback).

liz: thanks team. I'll update internal channels once we hit 60m stable window. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Closing actions: support follow-ups, postmortem, customer RCA.

mike: resolved for now — leaving thread open until 60m clean window.

liz: noted. closing when no regressions. :white_check_mark:
